## Track I: isoenergetic KAM, confinement, restricted three-body problem

### isoenergetic_kam

[`KAM.Iso.isoenergetic_kam`](../KAM/Frozen/Iso/Theorems/IsoenergeticKam.lean#L44) · ✅ proved and sealed

I-G1: canonical isoenergetic a-posteriori KAM, HL19 Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.7. Uniformization fixes the ray, its endpoint margin, and an upper bound for gamma first. The energy conclusion is pointwise, by invariance and nonresonance, not merely averaged.

- **Source:** HL19 Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.7, pp. 18–19 (statement.md §I-G1)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Iso.IsoenergeticKam`
- **Manifest ID:** `iso.isoenergetic_kam.v1`

### all_time_confinement

[`KAM.Iso.all_time_confinement`](../KAM/Frozen/Iso/Theorems/AllTimeConfinement.lean#L45) · ✅ proved and sealed

I-HEAD: all-time action confinement in two degrees of freedom, derived from I-G1, energy-cylinder separation and ODE continuation; not a verbatim HL19 theorem. Every local solution through the initial point agrees with the exhibited global one.

- **Source:** statement.md §I-HEAD (our deduction: KAM tori separate the energy surface)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Iso.AllTimeConfinement`
- **Manifest ID:** `iso.all_time_confinement.v1`

### kepler_bordered_det

[`KAM.Iso.kepler_bordered_det`](../KAM/Frozen/Iso/Theorems/KeplerBorderedDet.lean#L43) · ✅ proved and sealed

- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Iso.KeplerBorderedDet`
- **Manifest ID:** `iso.kepler_bordered_det.v1`

### restricted_near_circular

[`KAM.Iso.restricted_near_circular`](../KAM/Frozen/Iso/Theorems/RestrictedNearCircular.lean#L48) · ✅ proved and sealed

I-R3BP: an open four-dimensional near-circular region, all of whose actual restricted three-body solutions are global, bounded and uniformly separated from both primaries. Derived application; not the numerical Victoria theorem of Celletti--Chierchia.

- **Source:** statement.md §I-R3BP (Arnold 1963; Chierchia 2005 (3.37); our deduction)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Iso.RestrictedNearCircular`
- **Manifest ID:** `iso.restricted_near_circular.v1`

### zero_perturbation

[`KAM.Nekhoroshev.zero_perturbation`](../KAM/Frozen/Nekhoroshev/Theorems/ZeroPerturbation.lean#L40) · ✅ proved and sealed

N-ZERO: exact all-time integrable dynamics. This is our explicit zero-perturbation supplement to BM Theorem 2.1 p. 5, whose printed strict bound excludes `ε = 0`.

- **Source:** statement.md §N-ZERO (our supplement; BM11 p. 1)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Nekhoroshev.ZeroPerturbation`
- **Manifest ID:** `nekhoroshev.zero_perturbation.v1`

### quasiConvex_nekhoroshev_complexBound

[`KAM.Nekhoroshev.quasiConvex_nekhoroshev_complexBound`](../KAM/Frozen/Nekhoroshev/Theorems/QuasiConvexNekhoroshevComplexBound.lean#L47) · ✅ proved and sealed

N-HEAD-C: a separate source-input variant using Pöschel 1993, Theorem 1, pp. 190--191. Both new bounds precede the constants. `Mcomplex` supplies the complex Hessian bound; `ωmin` supplies quantitative quasi-convexity and excludes Theorem 1's low-frequency exception. The frequency upper bound required by its time prefactor follows from the retained real `B(M)`. All conversions and source-line anchors are given in docs/tracks/N/sources.md. This is a new proposal; the approved N-HEAD declaration above is unchanged.

- **Source:** Pöschel 1993 Theorem 1, pp. 190–191, via BM11 Theorem 2.1, p. 5 (statement.md §N-HEAD-C)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Nekhoroshev.QuasiConvexNekhoroshevComplexBound`
- **Manifest ID:** `nekhoroshev.quasiConvex_nekhoroshev_complexBound.v1`

### partialConvex_nekhoroshev

[`KAM.Nekhoroshev.partialConvex_nekhoroshev`](../KAM/Frozen/Nekhoroshev/Theorems/PartialConvexNekhoroshev.lean#L48) · ✅ proved and sealed

N-PARTIAL-CONVEX. Fixed h, complex Hessian bound and domains precede the threshold, which is uniform in the normalized perturbation and supplied interval. The slow-domain condition is tested only through the queried time, never assumed through the exponential window. Source: Nekhoroshev 1977, Theorem 4.4, p. 30. The enlarged source tube contains the working domain with a fixed collar. Use the definite-Hessian proof of Lemma 10.6, then the printed proof of Theorem 4.4; do not assert literal global source steepness at boundary centres. See notes.md.

- **Source:** N-PARTIAL-CONVEX: Nekhoroshev 1977 Theorem 4.4 p. 30 with Remarks 4.5.A–B, convex specialization on the enlarged fast domain
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Nekhoroshev.PartialConvexNekhoroshev`
- **Manifest ID:** `nekhoroshev.d25.partialConvex_nekhoroshev.v1`

### averaging_mean

[`KAM.Nekhoroshev.averaging_mean`](../KAM/Frozen/Nekhoroshev/Theorems/AveragingMean.lean#L44) · ✅ proved and sealed

N-AVERAGING-MEAN, analytic Hamiltonian specialization of AKN06 p.243 (6.27)--(6.28). AKN Theorem 6.11 and Corollary 6.1 for genuine solution families. The flow premise is only typing/existence on the stated interval; there is no hypothesis about its error or about an exceptional set. Constants are chosen after the fixed analytic system and compact initial set, before ε, the solution family, and κ. Measure is unnormalized phase volume.

- **Source:** AKN06 Theorem 6.11 (6.27), p. 243; Nei76 Theorem 1
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Nekhoroshev.AveragingMean`
- **Manifest ID:** `nekhoroshev.d28.averaging_mean.v1`

### averaging_most

[`KAM.Nekhoroshev.averaging_most`](../KAM/Frozen/Nekhoroshev/Theorems/AveragingMost.lean#L44) · ✅ proved and sealed

N-AVERAGING-MOST, derived from AKN06 p.243 and Neishtadt 1976 pp.1295--1298. Local-domain, actual-solution consequence of AKN (6.28). Existence and confinement are conclusions on the good data, not premises. The source smoothness convention is AKN06 p.3 footnote 1; the averaged-orbit collar is Remark 6.4, pp.217--218. Neishtadt Theorem 2 includes existence in its good-data definition; notes.md gives the stopped proof plan and corrects the maximum-error step. No flow or future confinement is assumed here.

- **Source:** AKN06 Corollary 6.1 (6.28), p. 243; Nei76 Theorem 2 (8), p. 1296
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Nekhoroshev.AveragingMost`
- **Manifest ID:** `nekhoroshev.d28.averaging_most.v1`

## Track P: planetary systems

### properlyDegenerateKAM

[`KAM.Planetary.properlyDegenerateKAM`](../KAM/Frozen/Planetary/Theorems/ProperlyDegenerateKAM.lean#L53) · ✅ proved and sealed

P-G v0.2: corrected specialization of CP11 Theorem 11.1 / CP10 Theorem 1.3. Audit P1-P3: oscillator discs, a fast diffeomorphism near closure V, and a boundary collar. These corrected hypotheses and joint analyticity await owner approval; see statement.md. All geometric and analytic data precede the two small parameters.

- **Source:** CP11 Theorem 11.1, pp. 50–51, and CP10 Theorem 1.3, as the corrected specialization of Q-P1 (statement.md §P-G)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Planetary.ProperlyDegenerateKAM`

### planarTwoPlanetKAM

[`KAM.Planetary.planarTwoPlanetKAM`](../KAM/Frozen/Planetary/Theorems/PlanarTwoPlanetKAM.lean#L47) · ✅ proved and sealed

P-PLANAR: analytic planar two-planet theorem, with moving Sun. CP09 Theorem 4 with Fejoz Proposition 77, using the recorded source-proof repairs. Fejoz erratum p.3 supplies the smooth counterpart. Only distinct ordered axes are assumed; no numerical separation threshold is taken from CP11 Section 8.1 (audit P4).

- **Source:** Féjoz 2004 Proposition 77 and CP09 Theorem 4 (statement.md §P-PLANAR)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Planetary.PlanarTwoPlanetKAM`
- **Manifest ID:** `planetary.planarTwoPlanetKAM.v1`

### fixedSunPlanetaryKAM

## Track R: Rüssmann's KAM theorem (weak non-degeneracy)

### russmann_kam

[`KAM.Russmann.russmann_kam`](../KAM/Frozen/Russmann/Theorems/RussmannKam.lean#L47) · ✅ proved and sealed

**R-HEAD.** Rüssmann's KAM theorem (Rus01 Thm 1.7, maximal case). Let `h` be real-analytic on a complex neighbourhood of a bounded connected open set `B ⊆ ℝⁿ` whose frequency map `ω = ∇h` is not contained in any hyperplane through the origin: `c · ω ≢ 0` on `B` for every `c ≠ 0`. Then there is a Diophantine exponent `τ > n - 1` such that, for every closeness `δ > 0`, every `κ > 0` and every sufficiently small real-analytic perturbation `f`, the invariant Lagrangian tori of `H = h + f` with `(γ, τ)`-Diophantine frequencies lying within `δ` of the unperturbed tori fill `Tⁿ × B` up to a set of volume at most `κ · vol(Tⁿ × B)`.

- **Source:** [Rus01](PAPERS.md#rus01), Theorem 1.7, p. 126, maximal case p = q = 0; §1.1-1.2 (non-degeneracy); deviations D-R1-D-R5 (statement.md §1)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Russmann.RussmannKam`
- **Manifest ID:** `russmann.russmann_kam.v1`

## Track B: finite-time effective stability (and SJSU gate 2)

### torus_confinement

[`KAM.EffectiveStability.torus_confinement`](../KAM/Frozen/EffectiveStability/TorusConfinement.lean#L33) · ✅ proved and sealed

**B1-T** (plan §2.2; GLS17 §4.3 (56)–(58)): finite confinement in a canonical cylinder. The physical phase coordinates are lifted real coordinates. Only the pullback Hamiltonian must be angle-periodic. The normal part is differentiated through `H ∘ Ψ - R`, which is differentiable on the open chart domain; no differentiability hypothesis on `N` is needed.

- **Source:** program-b-plan §2.2 (B1-T); GLS17 §4.3 (56)–(58)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.EffectiveStability.TorusConfinement`
- **Manifest ID:** `effectiveStability.d72.torus_confinement.v1`

### oscillator_confinement

[`KAM.EffectiveStability.oscillator_confinement`](../KAM/Frozen/EffectiveStability/OscillatorConfinement.lean#L34) · ✅ proved and sealed

**B1-E** (plan §2.3; CL20 §4.1 (32)–(37)): Cartesian oscillator confinement, including zero actions. Coordinates are `w = (q, p)`, with action `KAM.Planetary.oscillatorAction w.2 w.1`, so `I_j = (p_j² + q_j²) / 2` and `{I_j, R} = q_j ∂_{p_j} R - p_j ∂_{q_j} R`. Rotation invariance of the differentiable function `H ∘ Ψ - R` gives the normal-part cancellation without differentiating `N`.

- **Source:** program-b-plan §2.3 (B1-E); CL20 §4.1 (32)–(37)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.EffectiveStability.OscillatorConfinement`
- **Manifest ID:** `effectiveStability.d72.oscillator_confinement.v1`

### henonHeiles_confinement

[`KAM.EffectiveStability.henonHeiles_confinement`](../KAM/Frozen/EffectiveStability/HenonHeilesConfinement.lean#L32) · ✅ proved and sealed

**Hénon–Heiles confinement** (track B, plan §4 "A first instance with literal acceptance criteria"; CL20 Appendix B model `H = I₁ - (√2/2) I₂ + q₁² q₂ - q₂³/3`, `q = z.1`, `p = z.2`): every initial point with both oscillator actions `≤ (1/12500)²` has a Hamiltonian solution on `(-T₁, T₁)` with `T₁ > 10¹⁰`, unique among solutions on intervals through `0`, whose actions stay `< 101/10¹⁰` and within `12/10¹⁰` of their initial values for `|t| ≤ 10¹⁰`.

- **Source:** program-b-plan §4 'A first instance with literal acceptance criteria' (HH); CL20 Appendix B
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.EffectiveStability.HenonHeilesConfinement`
- **Manifest ID:** `effectiveStability.d73.henonHeiles_confinement.v1`

### sjsu_secular_confinement

[`KAM.EffectiveStability.sjsu_secular_confinement`](../KAM/Frozen/EffectiveStability/SJSU/SecularConfinement.lean#L42) · ✅ proved and sealed

**SJSU secular confinement** (T2-CONF, D74/D75; `docs/explorations/sjs-rigor-plan.md` §1.1): for every initial state within `10⁻⁶` (sup norm in `(ξ, η)`) of the nominal secular state (SLG13 Table 1 read as Poincaré elements and mapped to secular variables, `applications/sjsu/validation/ table2_map_poincare_order1.json`), `SJSU18-O2` has a solution on `(-T₁, T₁)` with `T₁ > 5·10⁹` yr, unique among solutions on intervals through `0`, along which for `|t| ≤ 5·10⁹` yr the fixed-reference secular-model eccentricities of Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus, `e_j = √(1 - (1 - Γ_j/Λ*_j)²)` with `Γ_j = (ξ_j² + η_j²)/2` and the dataset's reference actions `Λ*_j` (at `L = 0`), stay in `[0.026, 0.062]`, `[0.009, 0.085]` and `[0.006, 0.063]`. Nothing is asserted about the osculating elements of the full planetary problem.

- **Source:** § "The theorem" (T2-CONF; docs/explorations/sjs-rigor-plan.md §1.1)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.EffectiveStability.SJSUSecularConfinement`
- **Manifest ID:** `effectiveStability.d76.sjsu_secular_confinement.v1`

## Magnetic field-line barrier (proof open)

### magnetic_barrier

[`KAM.Magnetic.magnetic_barrier`](../KAM/Frozen/Magnetic/Theorems/MagneticBarrier.lean#L41) · ⬜ not yet

**Magnetic transport barrier.** The field-line flow of the controlled model at `ε = 3/2500` has a real-analytic invariant graph `p = P(q, φ)`, one-periodic in both angles, with `8/25 ≤ P ≤ 39/100`, which no field line crosses: every initial point has a global field line, which every local field line through it on an interval containing `0` agrees with, and the side of the graph (below, on, above) is the same at every real time. The graph is the action component of an analytic primary invariant torus `K∞` of the extended Hamiltonian `magHamC`, holomorphic on the strip of width `3/1000000`, real on real angles, with frequency `(α, 1)` (`α = magAlpha`), energy zero and clock `φ = θ₁` (plan-magnetic-barrier §1.2).

- **Source:** FREEZE-PROPOSAL §Proposed Lean text, draft/MagneticBarrier.lean.txt (headline)
- **Proof assembled in:** `KAM.Provider.Magnetic.MagneticBarrier`
- **Manifest ID:** `magnetic.magnetic_barrier.v1`
